newsitem.title: KENYA: Biwott, once murder suspect, rejoins Kenyan cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Biwott, once murder suspect, rejoins Kenyan cabinet.

text.p: Nicholas Biwott, named by British detectives as a prime suspect in the 1990 murder of Foreign Minister Robert Ouko, returned to Kenya's cabinet on Wednesday.

A powerful member of parliament and confidant of President Daniel arap Moi, Biwott was sacked as industry minister in 1991 after allegations of corruption were made against him at a judicial inquiry into Ouko's murder.

British detective John Troon named Biwott as one of two "prime" suspects in Ouko's death, along with former powerful civil servant Hezekiah Oyugi. Government official Jonah Anguka was named as a "peripheral" suspect.
Moi abruptly closed the inquiry after its focus appeared to shift to corruption and ordered police, whom Troon accused of obstructing his independent inquiry, to complete a probe.
Police arrested Biwott, Oyugi and Anguka but released Biwott and Oyugi for lack of evidence. Anguka was tried and found not guilty.
Biwott, 54, was nicknamed "Godfather" and is often referred to by Nairobi newspapers as Moi's right-hand man. Biwott named himself the "total man" in recognition of his immense powers.
Biwott labelled the charges of corruption and involvement in the Ouko murder "foreign propaganda" and has persistently denied involvement.
"I am innocent. Even I really want to know who killed Ouko. He was a good and able man," Biwott once told parliament.
Biwott's return to a full cabinet posting indicated Moi had completed his line-up for presidential and parliamentary elections due this year.
Moi also demoted Simeon Nyachae, a powerful politician widely seen as a potential vice-presidential candidate against incumbent George Saitoti -- a professor of mathematics and Biwott confidant.
He sacked Kipkalya Kones and demoted William Ole Ntimama, who had been associated with a group in Moi's ruling KANU party who wanted party elections so Nyachae could challenge Saitoti.
Biwott has led a group of politicians who were opposed to KANU elections and favoured Saitoti as vice-president until after national elections.
At the Ouko inquiry, the sister of the murdered foreign minister had said Ouko told her Biwott was dangerous and synonymous with corruption.
Financial analysts say Biwott has invested heavily in real estate in and outside Kenya. They cited him as the main reason Western donors refused to aid the energy sector when he was in cabinet.

Early in 1991, the U.S. bank Citibank NA almost left Kenya after he refused to repay a $12.5 million loan. The affair was settled after Western ambassadors warned Moi that private investment would be driven away if the money was not paid.
Financial analysts said on Wednesday donors would put a new focus on corruption and accountability because they did not trust Biwott.
Biwott, a member of Moi's Kalenjin tribe, was Moi's personal assistant and business manager when Moi was vice-president between 1969 and 1978.
After Moi took over on the death of founding president Jomo Kenyatta in 1978, Biwott rose quickly as Moi surrounded himself with politican novices who gave him absolute loyalty.
Little is known about Biwott's personal life. He graduated in economics from Melbourne University, is married to an Austrian and has two daughters.
